newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Bayer unit to plead guilty to price fixing - sources.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Bayer unit to plead guilty to price fixing - sources.

text.p: A U.S. subsidiary of Bayer AG has agreed to plead guilty to criminal charges in a government price-fixing investigation of food additives and pay a large fine, sources close to the case said Wednesday.
The fine is expected to be tens of millions of dollars.
The subsidiary, Haarmann & Reimer Corp., of Springfield, N.J., had already paid $46 million in a separate civil settlement involving citric acid, reached in December.
The probe grew out of an initial investigation of Archer-Daniels-Midland Co. which has already pleaded guilty and paid a record $100 million fine.

The Haarmann & Reimer fine, which is expected to total more than $40 million, will be the second largest criminal antitrust fine, after the ADM settlement. A Justice Department spokesman declined to comment on the case.
The plea was expected to be entered in federal court in San Francisco, where the earlier civil case was settled.
In that case four companies, including Haarmann & Reimer and ADM, agreed to pay a total of $94 million to settle a class-action lawsuit filed by bottlers and processors.

The suit accused the companies of meeting secretly around the world to fix prices and divide up shares in the market for citric acid. Citric acid is a corn-based preservative and flavoring agent with sales worth more than $1 billion a year.
